      <!-- Main Content -->
      <div class="about-content">
        <div class="about-text">
          <p>
            This website at its heart is an attempt to build a website I would like to read. I am an avid golf researcher with an interest in robotics and the mechanics of linked systems. After scouring the web for resources I finally came to the realization that I could just build the website I was looking for with the articles and resources that I was trying to track down.
          </p>
          
          <p>
            Rather than trying to organize my notes offline across multiple devices and formats, why not collect them together in a unified place where others who are also interested can find value in them. To achieve this goal, I have leaned heavily on the assistance of AI models in developing and troubleshooting code and building the website.
          </p>
          
          <p>
            Rather than curate the website myself, I have outlined articles and topics I would like to build or resources that I would like to see and then fed them to AI and importantly - iterated to improve quality. While much of AI-generated golf content can end up as correlational gibberish, there can be significant value when you know how to use it right.
          </p>
          
          <p>
            Rather than asking it for answers, ask it to provide mathematical expressions that can be validated. Ask it to write code that can be reviewed. Ask it to track down sources and links for further information. Every time an article is posted, it is then reviewed by automated bots overnight and feedback is given in the morning. It has been a fun process setting up guardrails to help AI give the most value.
          </p>
          
          <p>
            The agents reviewing the site have different personas. There are editors attempting to improve the fluidity and prose. There is a curator coming up with new topics or avenues to explore. There is a librarian at work in the background curating a cross-linked bibliography of all of the sources that are available. There are mathematicians and mechanics scouring the equations and validating and debugging them.
          </p>
          
          <p>
            Importantly, there are also critics. My goal here is not to hide weakness, but identify it and explore it. The edge cases and shortcomings of a given paradigm often hold extreme value. There is an agent to defend and shore up any technical shortcomings identified by the critics.
          </p>
          
          <p>
            By no means is the website intended to be exhaustive or comprehensive. It is just a place to store resources for myself and construct a technical argument towards the understanding of the viewpoint of the golf swing that I have developed through my years of study. This argument and the site are not complete, nor will they ever be. They will evolve and adapt when new information is identified.
          </p>
          
          <p>
            If this information is of interest to you, feel free to use and share however you choose. I don't care too much about citations personally, but if the information comes from other authors whose work I have linked here, please give credit where credit is due.
          </p>
          
          <p>
            Researching the golf swing is an often fruitless endeavor where you will encounter more than your fair share of critics. An atta boy or tip of the cap to those providing research into the topics we are all mutually interested in is in order when you find something to help you on your way.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
